newsitem.title: USA: Occidental lawyers review records - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Occidental lawyers review records - WSJ.

text.p: Lawyers for Occidental Petroleum Corp have examined records involving its dealings with government agencies and businessmen in a number of countries to determine if it overpaid some foreign middlemen or whether any money was used for foreign payoffs, the Wall Street Journal said.

In its electronic edition on Monday, the Journal said the lawyers have looked at records involving Occidental's dealings in Congo, Qatar, Bangladesh, Yemen, Malaysia and Russia, as well as other countries.
The Journal, citing unnamed sources it said were familiar with the matter, said the inquiry has found instances of questionable overseas transactions and lax financial procedures.

It said that Occidental has since tightened financial controls and implemented a new code of conduct restricting the use of "unwritten side contracts," offshore companies, numbered bank accounts and other practices.
Occidental Petroleum was not immediately available for comment on the Journal article.

The Journal said the lawyers have concentrated on who authorised consulting payments and "finders fees" that some current and former company executives contend were not linked to identifiable services.

In addition, the lawyers have focused on some apparent discrepancies between the contract language signed by some middlemen and the work they performed for Occidental, the Journal quoted unnamed sources as saying.
George Nolley, chairman of the audit committee, told the Journal that a review of Occidental's financial practices has taken place and that the board has moved to strengthen internal controls.
